_what: The EEAF data model every person's record store keeps, as DATA read by src/record-engine.mjs and passed to parts/record-log (record-model.mjs, invariant 11 of record-log-store.mjs). A record's type is its entity type; its top-level fields are the type's properties (every property a record ever holds is seen and kept, declared or not, with the value kinds it held); `kinds` declares, for a type, the value kind of some properties (a live write that sets one to another kind is refused, model_refused) and its `parts`: participation, a record holding another thing under a role at `path` (an id, a list of ids, or a list of objects whose `each` path names the id; a list's members in order are an interaction set), so what holds any id is one range of keys (holdersOf). `value_kinds` says what each value kind is: `is` a string, number, boolean, object, list or id (a non-empty text without '/'), or `list_of` one of those; a kind with neither checks nothing. `declared_by` names records that declare kinds themselves: a list declares `record:<row_type>`, each of its fields a property of the value kind its field kind holds (src/lists.json field_kinds `value`, filled in by src/record-engine.mjs), and a field holding row ids a participation role over them. A kind's `erasable` fields are kept sealed under a key of each record's own, so erasing the record (erase_record) deletes the key and every copy of their words with it; its `erasable_key` names the field of the record whose words they are, sealed under that record's key so erasing it reaches them at once (an arrival's message, a job's message); its `erase_with` names the records that hold the same words and are erased with it (a record named from its id, by one of its fields, or through a declared index of another kind), followed from each in turn. A kind's `erase_action` ({ label, glyph, confirm }) is how a screen offers erasing one of its records to the person: a secondary action that asks `confirm` once in place, then calls erase_record (src/workspace/messages-screen.tsx). A new kind, property or part is a row here (or, for a person's own kinds, a list they make), never code.

relations._what: Relations (src/record-model-tools.mjs relate, the relate_records tool): participation between any two things with the role as data. `self` is the record id `me` names (the person whose store it is); a subject or object `<entity kind>:<name>` is an entity record of that kind, made once by its name. Each relation keeps a fractional order key per side (subject_order among the subject's relations of that role, object_order among the object's), so each end orders its links on its own, and `alive` (false: ended, kept with its places so relating it again puts it back where it was). `side_most` is how many relations of one end and role are read to place a new one.

activities._what: Activities (src/record-model-tools.mjs relate, the relate_records tool's `activities`; read with read_model `history`): one record per thing that happened between people (an email, a call, a meeting, a message, an introduction, a note), with when it was (`at`, ISO), a few words, and every record that took part, each under a role of its own (a sender, a caller, an attendee). It is named by what it is (kind, time, source and who took part), so saying it again changes nothing. A person's history, a pair's shared history and when they were last in touch are filters over these records through the one `participant` part, never notes kept on the person. `kinds` and `participant_roles` are every word allowed; `participants_most` is how many may take part in one; `history_most` is how many an ordered history read goes through; `summary_most` is the longest summary.
